requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today and All smart rows plus six coloured lists, each with its open count. Counts update after changes (Home 25→24, All 135→134).

Open tasks come first, then a 'Completed (n)' section header with a chevron that collapses and expands; the collapsed state survives relaunch. The round checkbox completes a task (green check) and reopens it, and the counts update.

The New Task sheet has an auto-focused title, notes, a Due Date switch with an inline graphical calendar, a Priority menu (None/Low/Medium/High) and a List picker. Tapping a row opens the same Details sheet; editing the title and priority saved correctly.
Overdue dates show a red '! Overdue · Wed, Oct 21' with an exclamation icon. High priority shows a red !!!; low and medium show grey ! and !!.
Native trailing swipe shows a full-height red Delete action, and deleting works. Long-press drag reorders, and the new order persisted across relaunch.
+ opens a New List alert with a text field. Swiping a list row offers Rename and Delete, and the ••• menu in a list has Rename List and Delete List. Deleting a list with tasks asks for confirmation.
After relaunch the completion, edit, new task, deletion, reorder, list changes and collapsed state were all still there.

tells: Reordering has no visible affordance (no grip and no Edit mode on the task list); you have to discover the long-press drag.
At the largest text size the floating Add List '+' button sits over the list rows.
Lists are created and renamed in a text-field alert rather than a sheet (acceptable, but Reminders uses a sheet).
A.scroll: A real UITableView/List feel: smooth slow drags and flings, no blank or popping rows, the large title collapses into the inline title correctly, and pulling past the top rubber-bands.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today, All and My Lists rows showing open counts; the counts update correctly. Every list icon is the same orange glyph.

Open tasks come first, then a 'Completed · n' row with a blue Show/Hide text button (collapsed by default, and the state persists). The checkbox completes and reopens tasks immediately, and the '25 open' subtitle updates.

The New Task form has a title, a Due Date switch with a compact date picker, a Priority menu, a List menu and Notes, and Save is disabled until there is a title. Tapping a task opens Details for editing; the edit saved.
Overdue dates are shown in red as 'Oct 21, 2026 · Overdue'. High priority shows a red !!!; low and medium are not marked.
Swiping a task reveals a Delete button, and deleting works. Dragging the always-visible grip handle reorders, and the order persisted across relaunch.
+ opens a New List sheet. Rename List and Delete List are in the ••• menu, with a confirmation alert. Swiping a list row offers Delete.
After relaunch the edits, new task, deletion, reorder and completion state were all still there.

tells: The task list is a custom scroll view, not a table: swiping a row reveals a small hand-drawn red pill with 'Delete' written underneath, instead of iOS's full-height swipe action.
Grip (≡) handles show on every row all the time, which no stock iOS list does outside edit mode, and they take width from the titles.
A populated list opens with a small centred title and an 'N open' subtitle, while an empty list or a pulled-down All screen shows a large title, so the title style is inconsistent.
The Completed section header is a grey label with a blue 'Show/Hide' text button rather than a native disclosure section header.
Every user list gets the same orange ≡ glyph, with no colour or icon per list.

At the largest text size the edit sheet's title is a single-line field that truncates ('Read the tax…'), the list's navigation title does not scale, and the task text wraps into a narrow column beside the grip.
The Due Date switch has no accessibility label (id only).
Dates always include the year ('Nov 16, 2026') instead of the relative or short formatting iOS apps use.
B.scroll: Scrolls smoothly with no blank rows or jumps, and fling and rubber-banding feel native, though the task list is a plain white scroll view, not a grouped table.

why: Both apps do everything the spec asks and keep it across relaunch, but A reads as a genuine Reminders-style UIKit/SwiftUI app: native swipe actions, a large title that collapses, a disclosure-style Completed section, per-list colours, an inline calendar and text that wraps properly at the largest size. B's task screen is visibly hand-built: a drawn swipe pill, always-on grip handles, an inconsistent title style, a Show/Hide text toggle, and a title field that truncates at large text.
